title: Inside Black Friday at Lowe’s: From the First Customers to the Tech Behind It
summary: Inside Black Friday at Lowe’s: From the First Customers to the Tech Behind It
body_markdown:
Before the doors opened at 6 a.m. on Black Friday, one of retail’s biggest days was already underway at Lowe’s.


Across the country, customers had been lining up for hours, bundled against the cold and waiting for the doors to open.


In North Carolina, Dominique Parrish arrived around 1:30 a.m. after his wife told him about Lowe’s Black Friday giveaway.


“It was freezing,” Parrish said. “I actually pulled up at 1 o’clock, realized that it was cold, went back to my house and put more clothes on.”


Parrish isn’t usually a Black Friday shopper, but the early wake-up paid off. He was one of the morning’s big winners, walking away with a new EGO outdoor power tool.


His wife, meanwhile, was still asleep.


“I just said, ‘I won,’” Parrish


said of


the text he sent her. The experience may have created a new tradition.


“Ten out of 10,” he said. “Now I’ll be here every year.”


Nearby, Michelle Abney arrived around 1:45 a.m. after her daughter, already waiting in line, called and told her to come.


Abney was shopping for a dishwasher. She ended up winning a Blackstone griddle and accessory, too.
